subject: Ceiling construct & annualization options for MSA/order form
messages:
From: Amira Khan <amira.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MSA - liability cap question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the clean draft. Legal has one major open item on limits of liability: they want us to agree a single aggregate cap for the full 3-year term instead of annualized buckets. Our procurement team is pushing for per-year resets to limit exposure during trials/bursts.

Can Redwood provide a few framing options (absolute cap, fee-multiplier, or annual reset) with the commercial trade-offs so execs can decide? We have a partner board review on Nov 23.

Best,
Amira

--
Amira Khan
Head of Procurement | Nimbus Analytics

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft MSA - liability cap question

Looping in Legal/Finance (Laura + Rishi) and AE (Stephanie). Nimbus asked for concrete framing options and economic tradeoffs. Quick thoughts below — will turn into a one-pager and proposed redlines attachment.

High-level constructs to present:
- Total-term aggregate cap: simplicity for buyers, predictable exposure for Redwood, tends to require a lower multiplier (e.g., 1x-2x of fees) because exposure can't compound annually.
- Annualized reset cap: reduces buyer's per-year risk and helps them keep initial committments lower; increases Redwood's aggregate exposure over long contracts (multiple of annual fees).
- Hybrid / tiered: per-year cap with an overall maximum cap across term (annual reset but bounded by absolute cap) — balances procurement concerns with provider protection.

Trade-offs to model: unit economics under bursty usage, worst-case indemnity scenarios, and whether security/data breaches carve-outs increase acceptable caps.

I'll drop a redline and a short memo by EOD. Thoughts?

-Karthik

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MSA - liability cap question

Karthik — good framing. From a legal risk perspective I prefer the hybrid approach but with clear carve-outs. Specific asks for the redline/memo: 

1) Proposed formula examples (we should show 1x, 2x, and 3x of fees paid in the preceding 12 months and the same expressed as total-term multiples).
2) A separate clause that excludes certain categories from the cap: (a) gross negligence/willful misconduct; (b) IP infringement claims; (c) third-party claims resulting from Redwood's persistence breach (we need to be careful about language here); (d) will propose narrow security/data incident carve-out for remediation costs.
3) Consequential damages: try to keep the broad consequential/indirect damages exclusion in place but list enumerated exceptions (e.g., breaches of confidentiality causing statutory penalties).

I will mark up MSA with clean language to reduce ambiguity. Also, point out to the buyer that multi-year ARR projections should be used when we propose multipliers to make sure the math is transparent.

-Laur a (in legal)

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Ceiling construct & annualization options for MSA/order form

Hi Amira — thanks for the note and context. Attached is a short one-pager and a redline (PDF) with 3 numeric scenarios so your execs can pick which risk profile they prefer. Quick summary in-line: 

Scenario A — Aggregate-term cap (recommended for enterprise deals): 2x fees paid in aggregate over the entire term, carve-outs as Laura suggested. Pros: simplest; conservative for Redwood. Cons: higher upfront multiplier for buyer.

Scenario B — Annual reset: cap = 1x fees paid in prior 12 months, resets each year. Pros: buyer-favorable and often accepted in procurement. Cons: under high growth/bursty usage, Redwood exposure could be ~N * annual cap.

Scenario C — Hybrid bounded: annual cap of 1x prior 12 months but overall cap equal to 2x aggregate fees across term. Pros: balance. Cons: slightly more complex wording.

Action items: 
- Amira: which scenario would procurement/executive committee prefer?
- Amira/Nimbus Legal: loop any internal counsel if they want alternate carve-outs.
- Karthik: if they pick B, we need an economics note showing worst-case UPL (unpaid liability) under their growth projections.

I've attached the redlines and the memo: "Redwood_proposed_redlines_20261113.pdf".

Thanks,
Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Account Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Amira Khan <amira.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@nimbus-analytics.com, procure@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ceiling construct & annualization options for MSA/order form

Stephanie / Karthik / Laura — appreciate the clear scenarios. Procurement is leaning toward Scenario B (annual reset) because it keeps budget lines predictable for the business unit. Legal is nervous about runaway aggregate exposure; I forwarded Laura's carve-out list to them. They're asking whether Redwood will accept a cap that is annual reset but constrained by a total-term maximum (i.e., Scenario C) as an internal compromise.

Two specific asks from their side:
1) Can you provide a short table showing the numeric exposure under Scenario B vs C using Nimbus's projected ARR (attached in their spreadsheet)?
2) Would Redwood accept a limited security incident carve-out that still caps remediation and third-party claims to a separate sub-cap (e.g., $5M) rather than removing them entirely from the ceiling?

We aim to finalize commercial terms by Nov 23 so the board packet can include the finalized liability section.

Best,
Amira

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Ceiling construct & annualization options for MSA/order form

Amira — thanks, that's helpful. We can accommodate Scenario C with the following constraints: 

- Annual reset cap = 1x fees paid in prior 12 months, resetting on each anniversary.
- Aggregate-term maximum = 2x total fees paid across the term (absolute ceiling).
- Security/data remediation & third-party claims: carve-out carved-in but limited — Redwood will accept remediation and third-party forensics costs up to a separate sub-cap of $5,000,000. Anything above that would go to standard indemnity channels and may be subject to negotiation.
- Consequential damages: maintain broad exclusion but explicitly preserve statutory damages and claims arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence.

I attached a clean redline (NIM_MSA_redline_20261114.docx) and a short exposure table reflecting Nimbus's ARR profile. Please confirm and we'll prepare a final execution-ready MSA for signature.

-Laur a
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
